bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical conflicts and global trade disruptions — Dependence on global supply chains for copper, aluminium, steel, semiconductors and specialized electrical components exposes transmission projects to procurement delays, input cost volatility, and execution risk; prolonged instability may disrupt logistics, raise freight costs and delay project timelines, impacting sector profitability.
- Execution delays and right-of-way (RoW) challenges — Land acquisition hurdles, forest/environment clearances and RoW disputes remain among the largest impediments to timely transmission project execution in India; industry estimates indicate RoW and statutory approval issues can delay commissioning by 6-18 months and raise project costs by 10%-20% in certain corridors.
- Grid stability risk from rapid renewable integration — The growing share of intermittent solar and wind generation creates challenges in frequency regulation, voltage stability, reactive power management and balancing peak/off-peak demand; without corresponding investment in flexible transmission systems, storage, FACTS devices and advanced grid controls, grid instability risks are expected to rise materially over the coming decade.
- Financial stress in state utilities / DISCOMs — Despite ongoing reforms, many state distribution companies continue to face financial stress affecting payment cycles and capital investment capability; aggregate outstanding dues owed by DISCOMs remain substantial, and delayed payments/weak utility finances can impact transmission project ordering, execution schedules and working capital requirements for equipment suppliers like the Company.
- Cybersecurity and digital infrastructure risk — As India's grid becomes increasingly digitalised (SCADA, WAMS, digital substations, smart meters, cloud-based grid software), cybersecurity risk is emerging as a major operational concern; the Indian power sector has witnessed a rising number of attempted cyber intrusions, and a successful breach of digital grid systems could cause operational disruption, data compromise, equipment damage and reputational risk.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: GE Vernova T&D India provides products and turnkey solutions for connecting and evacuating power from generation sources onto the grid, spanning power transformers, reactors, circuit breakers, gas insulated and air insulated switchgears, instrument transformers, substation automation equipment, digital software solutions, FACTS and HVDC systems, and substation engineering/construction and maintenance support. Customers span government and private power generation, transmission and distribution utilities as well as industrial clients in metals, mining and oil & gas, served through 5 domestic manufacturing sites and exports to 65 countries.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Power Transmission & Distribution Equipment:** Power transformers, Reactors (incl. Air-core Reactors), Circuit breakers (incl. live tank circuit breakers), Gas insulated switchgears (GIS), Air insulated switchgears (AIS), Instrument transformers (Current Transformers, Electromagnetic Voltage Transformers), Substation automation equipment, SF6-free switchgear (g³ technology, 145kV & 420kV), Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS) / STATCOM, High Voltage DC (HVDC) systems incl. LCC valves and VSC STATCOM valves, Bushings, Maintenance support
- **Digital & Software Solutions:** GridOS® (modular digital grid software platform), GridOS® ADMS (distribution management system), GridOS® DDLR (Digital Dynamic Line Rating), Digital Twin (virtual replica of grid assets), Asset Performance Management (APM) suite, FACTSFlex (digitally enabled STATCOM with monitoring/analytics)
- **Turnkey Solutions:** Substation engineering, construction and turnkey project execution

outlook.body: GE Vernova T&D India operates with 5 manufacturing sites (labour relations are separately noted at the Hosur, Padappai, Pallavaram and Vadodara units), which the Company describes as making it 'future ready to meet the industry's growing demand for grid equipment and services.' The Company states it is investing in manufacturing expansion, localization, and advanced technology capabilities, citing recent investments in HVDC valves, controls, and FACTS compensation technologies to strengthen readiness to address India's evolving grid requirements in renewable integration, grid stability, and high-capacity transmission corridors. This bundle does not disclose specific new project names, capacity quantum, or completion timelines for these investments.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's power sector entering a multi-year investment upcycle driven by rising electricity demand, energy transition goals, industrial growth and infrastructure expansion
- Peak power demand projected to rise from 245.4 GW in FY2025-26 to 366 GW by 2030 and further to ~459 GW by 2035-36, necessitating transmission infrastructure expansion
- India's target of 500 GW non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030 (expanding to ~786 GW by 2035-36) driving large-scale renewable integration and grid expansion investment
- Central Electricity Authority transmission roadmap targets development of over 900 GW of transmission network capacity by FY2035-36, with estimated investments of nearly ₹7.9 trillion by 2036
- Approximately ₹5 trillion of transmission projects currently under bidding or execution in India, reflecting near-term execution momentum
- Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) framework expanding the addressable market for transmission developers, EPC players and equipment suppliers
- Large-scale substation modernization (digital protection/control, SCADA, IEDs, GIS/hybrid substations) driving demand for grid equipment and digital solutions
- National Electricity Plan targets addition of ~33 GW of new HVDC bipole capacity by 2032, nearly doubling India's existing HVDC base, expected to drive strong demand for HVDC equipment
- Smart grid and digitalization opportunity under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with over 100 million smart meters installed or awarded for deployment
- Renewable generation increasingly concentrated in resource-rich, load-deficit regions creating structural need for interstate evacuation corridors, pooling substations and HVDC systems
- Order bookings expanded to ₹147.8 billion in FY2025-26, up 37% over the previous financial year
- Significant orders secured for both projects and equipment - transformers, reactors, 765 kV GIS, air-insulated switchgear (AIS) and grid automation systems
- Key HVDC project wins in FY2025-26: the 2.5 GW VSC-based Khavda-South Olpad HVDC project and the 2x500 MW Chandrapur HVDC refurbishment project
- Exports accounted for 33% of the Company's revenue and 8% of the total order book in FY2025-26, with new geographies added in Europe, South-East Asia, Middle East and Africa

open.item: Board recommended a final dividend of 500% (₹10 per equity share of face value ₹2) for FY2025-26, taking total payout to approximately ₹2,560.5 million, subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing Annual General Meeting.

Board sanctioned an investment of ₹1.4 billion to establish a new manufacturing line at the existing Chennai facility for LCC HVDC valves and VSC STATCOM valves, part of a three-year (2026-2028) capex programme funded through internal accruals.

Board sanctioned an investment of ₹8.1 billion to expand capacity across core product lines: Transformer and Reactor capacity at Vadodara to grow by more than 50%, GIS and AIS capacity at Hosur and Padappai to expand by approximately 25%, plus new dedicated manufacturing lines for Air-core Reactors and Bushings at Hosur; expected completion over 2026-2028, funded through internal accruals.
Company maintains a disciplined, selective approach to order intake, prioritizing margin-accretive opportunities and quality of backlog over pure volume expansion.

Company continues to expand localization and manufacturing capabilities under the 'Make in India' initiative to strengthen its ability to deliver globally competitive solutions from India for domestic and international markets.
Company is focused on maximizing output from existing factories via deployment of lean manufacturing lines, robotics, and advanced automation to enhance productivity and throughput.

Company is investing in manufacturing expansion, localization, and advanced technology capabilities, including recent investments in HVDC valves, controls, and FACTS compensation technologies to address India's evolving grid requirements.
